scenes.narration: Share the proof. Keep the measurements private. Bacchiri combines Midnight and Cloudflare to add verifiable evidence to measurement reports shared between organizations.

The measurement owner holds sensitive records. The verifier needs the date, the conditions, and the result. Bacchiri works with existing devices and cloud services. Our first business focus is measurement reporting on construction sites, followed by a partner pilot.

Connect your Wallet, review the details, and approve. Register the Device. Aggregate the daily measurements. Request a zero-knowledge proof. Approve and submit the transaction. Then let a third party verify the result. These five use cases form one connected workflow.

Authenticate with your connected Wallet and register the Device and its public threshold Policy. Review the registration details in your Wallet and approve. Before measurement begins, this links the Device to the conditions that apply and the period when they take effect.

The measurement owner aggregates one day of records into twenty-four hourly slots. Check the operational date and sample count, then prepare the private proof inputs. Raw measurements and actual hourly values stay separate from the public output. The verifier receives only the required results.

Request a proof for a completed operational day. Use the Job ID to follow acceptance, proof generation, and transaction preparation. Acceptance is not completion. Keep the page open while the job progresses. When the Device transaction is ready, the workflow asks for Wallet approval.

Review the transaction in your Wallet and approve the Device's transaction. The service's Sponsor Wallet adds the DUST fee to that approved transaction and submits it. Check the record on Midnight, then use the same Job ID to trace its transaction identifier.

The verifier uses the shared transaction identifier to check the public evidence. Review the operational date, hourly results, applicable Policy, and record on Midnight. The verifier can confirm the result and its supporting evidence without receiving the original measurement values.

The workflow covers normal days, out-of-range measurements, missing data, and rejected inputs. Out-of-range values do not become successful results. Missing hours are not filled in. Verifiers can distinguish a failed condition from a lack of information.

The Managed API connects existing cloud services. Register the measurement source and its Policy, then follow daily retrieval, proof generation, and submission. The service Wallet performs authorized operations, adding public verification to an existing measurement workflow.

The operations dashboard shows service health, daily metrics, and processing events. Follow proof processing and Wallet status, then investigate jobs that need attention. Operational information stays separate from secrets, while giving the team what it needs to keep the service running.

This diagram explains the implementation. Cloudflare manages requests and jobs. Proof generation and the Wallet run in separate containers. Raw measurement streams stay at the source. Private proof inputs are processed by the trusted backend.

The Wallet starts when work is needed, restores its encrypted state, and synchronizes. Once ready, it processes one job at a time, saves its state, and stops. This example starts daily processing at two a.m. It does not guarantee when a transaction will be confirmed.

The proof establishes the relationship between submitted private hourly inputs and the registered conditions. Physical sensor accuracy, measurement completeness, and correct aggregation need separate assurances. The current architecture trusts the backend and proof service.

Next, we will evaluate daily verification in a partner's real workflow, measuring reliability, support effort, and customer value. We will agree on the temperature measurement use case, evaluation period, and success metrics, then assess continued use and the conditions for commercial delivery.
